sections.preamble: You are a coding assistant running inside pi, a coding agent harness. Help users inspect files, run commands, and modify code.
sections.tools:
<tools>
- read: Read file contents
- bash: Execute bash commands (ls, grep, find, etc.)

Additional tools may be available.
</tools>
sections.rules:
<rules>
- Use bash for file operations like ls, rg, find
- Use read to examine files instead of cat or sed.
- You can inspect PI_* environment variables for current model and session details.
- Be concise in your responses
- Show file paths clearly when working with files
</rules>

toolsAdded.name: read
toolsAdded.description: Read the contents of a file. Supports text files and images (jpg, png, gif, webp, bmp). Images are sent as attachments. For text files, output is truncated to 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). Use offset/limit for large files. When you need the full file, continue with offset until complete.

path.description: Path to the file to read (relative or absolute)

offset.description: Line number to start reading from (1-indexed)

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to read

toolsAdded.name: bash
toolsAdded.description: Execute a bash command in the current working directory. Returns stdout and stderr. Output is truncated to last 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). If truncated, full output is saved to a temp file. Optionally provide a timeout in seconds.

timeout.description: Timeout in seconds (optional, no default timeout)

toolsAdded.name: phase_tracker
toolsAdded.description: Track workflow phase progress (brainstorm → plan → implement → verify → ship); ad-hoc calls do not arm gates. Not for ad-hoc use.

phase.description: Phase name (required for start, complete, skip)

reason.description: Reason (required for skip and grant_fix_rounds; for grant, the human's approval quoted)

rounds.description: Extra fix rounds the human explicitly approved (grant_fix_rounds only)

force.description: Reset and re-start a phase that is already complete or skipped (rare; default false)

substep.description: Substep label for action=substep on an in_progress phase; null or omitted clears it

toolsAdded.name: plan_tracker
toolsAdded.description: Track progress while EXECUTING an implementation plan (the implement phase), a verify-phase conformance fix wave, or another bounded gate checklist (e.g. pre-merge PR verification). Statuses: pending (not yet touched), in_progress (started; several at once is fine), complete, failed (terminal-negative: ran and did not pass; never counted done), skipped (terminal: not applicable in this run; counted done). Rule: pending tasks must trail every started or finished task - an update that would leave a pending task ahead of a non-pending one is rejected with the fix. update never sets pending; init and add do. Actions: init (set task list; elements are task-name strings or { name, status } to recreate a list with known statuses), add (append tasks as pending; existing statuses preserved), update (change task status), status (show current state), clear (remove plan), refresh (derive tasks from an artifact path while retaining other tasks). Do NOT use for brainstorming, research, or planning checklists: those phases are open-ended and a bounded task list misrepresents them as a fixed N-step process.

path.description: Artifact path for refresh; relative paths resolve against the session cwd

status.description: Status to recreate the task with (init only)

tasks.description: Tasks for init and add. A string is a pending task. init also accepts { name, status } to recreate a list with known statuses (fresh session, amendment re-init); the whole list must satisfy the pending-suffix rule.

status.description: New status (for update). failed is terminal-negative (ran and did not pass); skipped is terminal, not applicable in this run, counted as done. pending is set only by init/add; to redo a task, reopen it as in_progress, or re-init with {name, status}[] to recreate a whole list.

toolsAdded.name: plan_check
toolsAdded.description: Deterministically verify an implementation plan against its spec (mechanical checks); a pass stamps the plan for implement-start.

planPath.description: Path to the implementation plan (absolute, or relative to cwd)

toolsAdded.name: gauntlet_setting
toolsAdded.description: Resolve merged piGauntlet.* settings (repo over preset); for skill use only.

key.description: Which gauntlet setting to resolve (merged repo-over-preset).

---
name: gauntlet-resume
description: Use when a human wants to continue an interrupted gauntlet flow in a fresh session - from a gauntlet-handoff brief (file, pasted, or picked from the default handoff directory), from a bare worktree that already holds a spec, or from a spec tracked on main (creates or reuses its worktree via `/skill:using-git-worktrees`). Human-only; the sole resume entry point. Restores phase/plan tracker state through the legal arming sequence, never infers approval.
disable-model-invocation: true
argument-hint: "[<brief-file> | <spec>.md | <worktree-name-or-path>]"
---

> **Related skills:** Continues into `/skill:writing-plans`, `/skill:subagent-driven-development`, or `/skill:verification-before-completion` depending on the restored stage. `/skill:brainstorming` is where new ideas go - a free-form prompt is not a resume input.

# Gauntlet Resume

## Overview

Re-enter an interrupted gauntlet flow in a fresh session. Three inputs: a handoff brief
produced by `/skill:gauntlet-handoff` (grammar in `reference/brief-contract.md`), a bare
worktree whose spec/plan artifacts are reconstructed into tracker state
(`reference/reconstruction.md`), a spec seed (`reference/seed.md`). Every check runs
before any tracker mutation; every stop names the offending path, field, or line.

**Announce at start (after the marker on marked messages):** "I'm using the gauntlet-resume skill to continue an interrupted flow."

## Boundaries

- Reads: anything.
- Writes: `phase_tracker` / `plan_tracker` state after every check passes and every
  human question is answered; the plan file, only through `reference/brief-contract.md`
  `## Plan repair`; the ledger through `reference/reconstruction.md` pending recovery and the loop driver's admission/repair contract; on the seed route, what `/skill:using-git-worktrees` writes. Never a spec copy, rename, or marker commit.
- Never: `git worktree add` directly; worktree creation by resume itself only on
  the seed route, only through `/skill:using-git-worktrees`; infer approval from
  artifact presence; restore
  gate history, closure-review evidence, or fix rounds; start a later phase directly
  (that does not arm the flow).

## Arguments

`/skill:gauntlet-resume [<token>] [<worktree>]` - zero to two positional tokens, plus
optional pasted text after the command line. Count tokens first; then first match wins.
Spec dirs resolve per `reference/reconstruction.md` "Candidates" (`flowGuards.specDirs`
precedence).

Read and apply [menu-layout](../brainstorming/reference/menu-layout.md) before presenting these options and before acting on a numeric reply.

For the discovery menu, start the message with the marker specified below. Start the message with `gauntlet: gate=gauntlet-resume/discovery`.
For no briefs and every stop route in the table, end without mutation. Start the message with `gauntlet: stuck` followed by the existing reason on that line.

| Input | Route |
|---|---|
| no tokens, no pasted text | discovery: `<tmpdir>` via `node -p "require('os').tmpdir()"`; candidates are the regular files directly under `<tmpdir>/pi-handoff/` ending `.md` (non-recursive) whose line 1 starts `# Handoff:`; sorted by mtime, newest first; displayed one per line as `<n>. <title line> - <worktree: field value> - <mtime ISO-8601>` with `worktree: unavailable` when the field is absent; the human picks `<n>` (a single candidate is still confirmed); none -> STOP "no handoff briefs found under <tmpdir>/pi-handoff" |
| pasted text, line 1 starts `# Handoff:` | brief |
| two tokens, first an existing file with line 1 `# Handoff:` | brief with worktree override: required when the brief's worktree field is `no`/`unavailable`/not a git repo; must equal the brief's worktree after `realpath` otherwise |
| two tokens, first a spec seed | stop: `a spec seed takes no worktree: <second token>` |
| one token, existing regular file, line 1 starts `# Handoff:` | brief |
| one token, existing regular file ending `.md`, `realpath` under `<primary>/<specDir>` | spec seed - `reference/seed.md` |
| one token, existing regular file, anything else | stop: `not a handoff brief and not under <specDirs>: <path>` |
| one token, existing directory that is a git worktree root (`git -C <dir> rev-parse --show-toplevel` equals its `realpath`) other than `<primary>` | worktree |
| one token, missing path (ends `.md` or contains a separator) | stop: `not found: <path>` |
| one token, bare name | worktree at `<primary>/.worktrees/<name>`; missing or not a git worktree -> entry check 2 stop |
| anything else | stop: "this is a new idea - run /skill:brainstorming" |

A relative token resolves against the session cwd; a bare `name.md` absent there is
tried at `<primary>/<specDir>/name.md` per resolved spec dir in order, first hit wins.
`<primary>` is the checkout owning `.worktrees/`:
`dirname "$(git rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-common-dir)"` run in the session
cwd - absolute from any primary subdirectory and from inside a linked worktree
(`--show-toplevel` would return the linked worktree there). A pasted brief that needs
an override uses the file form. A brief then runs entry checks 1-6, so a stale or
foreign-repo brief stops there.

## Entry checks

For an entry-check stop, start with the terminal marker and retain the offending path, field, or line. Start the message with `gauntlet: stuck` followed by the reason on that line.

In order. All before any tracker mutation; entry check 1 is read-only. A spec
seed runs check 1 here, then `reference/seed.md`, which runs check 3 itself;
checks 2, 4, 5 do not apply; check 6 runs on the seed's pinned spec path.

1. **Idle session.** `phase_tracker({ action: "status" })`. Any phase not pending ->
   stop: "session already carries flow state - reset is your call".
2. **Target worktree.** Resolve from the brief's `worktree:` field, the override, or the
   bare argument. Stops: path missing or `git -C <path> rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree`
   fails; override and brief worktree differ after `realpath`; brief has no
   `## Repo state` heading (prefix match: `## Repo state` or
   `## Repo state: not a git repo`); brief worktree is `no`, `unavailable`, or
   `not a git repo` and no override was given - except a `worktree: no` brief **without**
   process state, which is the brainstorming route in Dispatch, not a stop. Other
   `unavailable` fields inside `## Repo state` are legal.
3. **Same-repository binding.** Settings and flow guards come from the repository in
   the extension's session cwd. Compare
   `realpath "$(git rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-common-dir)"` in the session
   cwd with
   `realpath "$(git -C <worktree> rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-common-dir)"`.
   If they differ, stop, name both paths, and say the resolved worktree belongs to a
   different repository; restart pi in that repository's primary checkout and re-run. For member-primary entry on a coordinated brief, also print `home is <repo>; restart there`, naming the run home.
   Same-repository worktrees proceed by path: use `git -C <worktree>` for
   worktree Git commands and absolute artifact paths for `Read` and `plan_check`.
3b. **Coordinated admission.** For a multi-member brief, read and apply `reference/brief-contract.md` "Coordinated admission" before any tracker write: resolve the home spec without inferring approval, compare ordered membership, validate each declared primary/common directory, shared branch and full home tuple, and live-validate receipts before admitting any missing tree. Preserve check 3's home binding.
4. **Drift notice.** Compare the brief's `HEAD` and `dirty` fields in `## Repo state`
   with the live worktree (`git -C <worktree> rev-parse HEAD`, `git -C <worktree>
   status --porcelain`). For coordinated briefs apply `reference/brief-contract.md` "Coordinated admission" per leg. Announce differences. Informational, never a stop.
5. **Skills loaded.** For each name in `## Skills loaded` (none for
   `## Skills loaded: none`): match against the frontmatter `name` of every
   `skills/*/SKILL.md` in this package; `Read` each match's complete file into the
   transcript; list non-matches as skipped. Loaded bodies are context only - no skill's
   entry actions run until Dispatch names one.
6. **Grant field.** Run deferred-header admission whenever a route resolves an existing spec, including brainstorm-stage process-state restore and reconstruction's unapproved-draft handoff, before any tracker mutation or brainstorming invocation. Carry the resolved `<spec path>` without re-resolving it: use `reference/brief-contract.md` "Process-state restore", `reference/reconstruction.md`, or the seed's pinned `<full-path>/<rel>` (`reference/seed.md`).
   Read the spec's header block (between the H1 and the first `##`). An exact `**Engine:** deferred` stops with `spec approved for handoff only - run brainstorming #N`; make no phase_tracker or plan_tracker mutation. After deferred-header admission, apply the grant predicate only for an approved spec in
   [Standing grants](../brainstorming/reference/amendment-surface.md#standing-grants): no
   `**Amend-grant:**` line -> no grant (legacy spec);
   exactly one line whose trimmed value is `none` -> no grant;
   exactly one line whose trimmed value is any other non-empty single-line text ->
   grant active, the sentence is that value;
   two or more lines, one line with an empty value, or a value continued onto the next physical line ->
   malformed, stop, print the offending line(s), no tracker call. Skip only grant decoding for routes that resolve no
   approved spec (hotfix, `worktree: no`, a brief whose active phase is brainstorm,
   reconstruction's unapproved-draft brainstorming handoff); print no grant line.
   Resume reports the line; it never writes it.

## Dispatch

For the `worktree: no` brainstorming offer, keep the explicit-selection wait. Start the message with exactly `gauntlet: question` on its own line, with no suffix.

| Input | Route |
|---|---|
| brief with `## Process state` | process-state restore - `reference/brief-contract.md` "Process-state restore" |
| brief without process state, `## Skills loaded` names `chase-bug` | hotfix route below, before any artifact reconstruction, no tracker calls |
| brief without process state, `worktree: no` | offer `/skill:brainstorming` with `## Intent` as the idea and wait for explicit selection; then invoke [`/skill:brainstorming`](../brainstorming/SKILL.md) in the current directory; resume creates no worktree - brainstorming's own Worktree First applies (a plain handoff is a new flow) |
| brief without process state, worktree present | `reference/reconstruction.md`, with `## Intent` and `## Decisions` carried into every confirmation prompt |
| bare worktree | `reference/reconstruction.md`; prompts state that no brief context is available (never invent Intent/Decisions) |
| spec seed | `reference/seed.md` |

**Hotfix route.** `skills/chase-bug/hotfix.md` consumes only a hotfix record at
`$TMPDIR/hotfix-<slug>.md`. If `## Decisions` or `## Intent` names an existing record
path, hand it to hotfix.md and skip its worktree-create step when the brief's worktree
exists (reuse it). Otherwise invoke `/skill:chase-bug` triage with `## Intent` to
re-derive the record.

## Post-restore continuation

A successful restore is an automatic handoff, not a terminal report; let the resumed skill own the next ask and its marker. Keep the brief fields unchanged and infer no approval. After citation repair of a plan that was dirty or untracked before repair, state explicitly that the repair stays in the working copy and lands with the next task commit; run no `git add` or repair commit, per `reference/brief-contract.md` "Citation repair".

After a successful restore, print the closing line from `reference/brief-contract.md`
(gate history not restored; the task to re-validate), then on its own line exactly one of `Standing grant active: <sentence>` or `No standing grant.` from check 6 (nothing when grant decoding was skipped), then continue in the stage's
owning skill **without** its reset-bearing entry:

| Active after restore | Continue in | Entry point |
|---|---|---|
| brainstorm | [brainstorming checklist](../brainstorming/SKILL.md#checklist) | on-disk state decides the step: draft marker on line 1 of the spec file -> step 4; spec title -> step 8. Never `/skill:brainstorming` entry (it resets both trackers) |
| approved spec with `**Engine:** loop`, no ledger | loop-implementation | after check 6, arm with `start brainstorm`, then `skip brainstorm resume: <spec path>` before driver admission; carry absolute worktree/spec paths and plan directory through Entry steps 1-5 per `reference/reconstruction.md` "Spec without plan": label Entry steps 1-5 explicitly in the response as Entry step 1: resolved settings; Entry step 2: verification; Entry step 3: driver's plan skip; Entry step 4: clean named-branch check and ledger creation; Entry step 5: `plan_check`, commit and implement start; no writing-plans body or task tracker initialization; refresh by ledger path after implement starts |
| plan with task engine | writing-plans body | skip its `start plan` call (already in_progress) |
| implement with line-1 ledger | loop-implementation | complete `reference/reconstruction.md` "Spec with ledger" ordered restore, cited by `reference/brief-contract.md`'s call table: entry checks 1-6, brainstorm start/skip, plan start/check/skip with reason `resume: <spec> (loop engine)`, implement start, pending recovery against the unmigrated ledger, clean-tree migration, final allowance validation, then one ledger-path refresh, no `init`; state the entire ordered sequence explicitly even when entry checks are already reported as passed; then continue at step 5 (`Before each dispatch`), applying the shared allowance boundary in reconstruction step 4 before continuation and preserving iterations/attempts/retry decisions; defer migration through missing-history or dirty-tree stops; reuse the existing ledger |
| implement with task plan | subagent-driven-development | re-validate `<task>` first (re-run its `Tests:`), then the task loop from the first non-complete task |
| verify with `Ledger:` (including ship-stage ledger briefs restored at verify) | /skill:loop-implementation | after `start verify`, restore the saved mixed task list with `init` as `reference/brief-contract.md` specifies, then pending recovery against the unmigrated ledger, clean-tree migration, final allowance validation and one ledger-path refresh through the shared allowance boundary in `reference/reconstruction.md` "Spec with ledger" step 4; legacy briefs without tasks omit init, not recovery/migration; render allowance and observed task/ledger state; read `After the loop` and its references; continue from `After the loop` step 1, the gate set per the loop skill's `## Gate set`; let that skill own execution, with no resume-owned gate run; retain whole-diff code review, happy path when triggered, fresh home conformance review and finishing; never start implement or synthesize Gn completion |
| verify without `Ledger:` | verification-before-completion | full conformance gate; nothing carried over |

## Red flags — STOP

- Any `phase_tracker` or `plan_tracker` mutation before the route's entry checks pass and
  every human question is answered.
- `start <phase>` for anything other than brainstorm as the first arming call.
- `complete` on a prior phase during restore (priors are `skip`ped with a `resume:` reason).
- Running `git worktree add` directly, or `cd`-ing to "fix" a cwd mismatch.
- Accepting a free-form prompt as a brief.

## Project overrides
If a gauntlet overrides file exists - checked in order:
`.pi/gauntlet-overrides.md`, `<repo root>/gauntlet-overrides.md`,
`<repo root>/doc/gauntlet-overrides.md`; first found wins - read it once per session - a skill that already has the file's content in context from an earlier skill's read skips the read; a restored session has nothing in context and reads it. Read
and apply `## conventions` whenever present, without a relevance
judgment.
Give this skill's named section precedence over conflicting
`## conventions` rules. Use other relevant sections - by name match,
by topic (routing,
verification, worktrees, etc.), or by workflow convention - to override or
extend the instructions above. Project-local `AGENTS.md` is already in
context - check it for project-specific routing tables, service paths, and
verification commands.

The recognized headings, their readers, and the rules an override cannot change are listed in the [configuration front door](../../README.md#project-specific-overrides); an override extends or replaces the step it names and never lifts this skill's HARD CONSTRAINT or MUST text.

produced by `/skill:gauntlet-handoff` (grammar in `reference/brief-contract.md`), a bare
worktree whose spec/plan artifacts are reconstructed into tracker state

before any tracker mutation; every stop names the offending path, field, or line.

## Boundaries

- Reads: anything.
- Writes: `phase_tracker` / `plan_tracker` state after every check passes and every
  human question is answered; the plan file, only through `reference/brief-contract.md`

optional pasted text after the command line. Count tokens first; then first match wins.

precedence).

For the `worktree: no` brainstorming offer, keep the explicit-selection wait. Start the message with exactly `gauntlet: question` on its own line, with no suffix.

| Input | Route |
|---|---|
| brief with `## Process state` | process-state restore - `reference/brief-contract.md` "Process-state restore" |
| brief without process state, `## Skills loaded` names `chase-bug` | hotfix route below, before any artifact reconstruction, no tracker calls |
| brief without process state, `worktree: no` | offer `/skill:brainstorming` with `## Intent` as the idea and wait for explicit selection; then invoke [`/skill:brainstorming`](../brainstorming/SKILL.md) in the current directory; resume creates no worktree - brainstorming's own Worktree First applies (a plain handoff is a new flow) |
| brief without process state, worktree present | `reference/reconstruction.md`, with `## Intent` and `## Decisions` carried into every confirmation prompt |
| bare worktree | `reference/reconstruction.md`; prompts state that no brief context is available (never invent Intent/Decisions) |
| spec seed | `reference/seed.md` |

**Hotfix route.** `skills/chase-bug/hotfix.md` consumes only a hotfix record at
`$TMPDIR/hotfix-<slug>.md`. If `## Decisions` or `## Intent` names an existing record
path, hand it to hotfix.md and skip its worktree-create step when the brief's worktree
exists (reuse it). Otherwise invoke `/skill:chase-bug` triage with `## Intent` to
re-derive the record.

## Post-restore continuation

A successful restore is an automatic handoff, not a terminal report; let the resumed skill own the next ask and its marker. Keep the brief fields unchanged and infer no approval. After citation repair of a plan that was dirty or untracked before repair, state explicitly that the repair stays in the working copy and lands with the next task commit; run no `git add` or repair commit, per `reference/brief-contract.md` "Citation repair".

After a successful restore, print the closing line from `reference/brief-contract.md`
(gate history not restored; the task to re-validate), then on its own line exactly one of `Standing grant active: <sentence>` or `No standing grant.` from check 6 (nothing when grant decoding was skipped), then continue in the stage's
owning skill **without** its reset-bearing entry:

| Active after restore | Continue in | Entry point |
|---|---|---|
| brainstorm | [brainstorming checklist](../brainstorming/SKILL.md#checklist) | on-disk state decides the step: draft marker on line 1 of the spec file -> step 4; spec title -> step 8. Never `/skill:brainstorming` entry (it resets both trackers) |
| approved spec with `**Engine:** loop`, no ledger | loop-implementation | after check 6, arm with `start brainstorm`, then `skip brainstorm resume: <spec path>` before driver admission; carry absolute worktree/spec paths and plan directory through Entry steps 1-5 per `reference/reconstruction.md` "Spec without plan": label Entry steps 1-5 explicitly in the response as Entry step 1: resolved settings; Entry step 2: verification; Entry step 3: driver's plan skip; Entry step 4: clean named-branch check and ledger creation; Entry step 5: `plan_check`, commit and implement start; no writing-plans body or task tracker initialization; refresh by ledger path after implement starts |
| plan with task engine | writing-plans body | skip its `start plan` call (already in_progress) |
| implement with line-1 ledger | loop-implementation | complete `reference/reconstruction.md` "Spec with ledger" ordered restore, cited by `reference/brief-contract.md`'s call table: entry checks 1-6, brainstorm start/skip, plan start/check/skip with reason `resume: <spec> (loop engine)`, implement start, pending recovery against the unmigrated ledger, clean-tree migration, final allowance validation, then one ledger-path refresh, no `init`; state the entire ordered sequence explicitly even when entry checks are already reported as passed; then continue at step 5 (`Before each dispatch`), applying the shared allowance boundary in reconstruction step 4 before continuation and preserving iterations/attempts/retry decisions; defer migration through missing-history or dirty-tree stops; reuse the existing ledger |
| implement with task plan | subagent-driven-development | re-validate `<task>` first (re-run its `Tests:`), then the task loop from the first non-complete task |
| verify with `Ledger:` (including ship-stage ledger briefs restored at verify) | /skill:loop-implementation | after `start verify`, restore the saved mixed task list with `init` as `reference/brief-contract.md` specifies, then pending recovery against the unmigrated ledger, clean-tree migration, final allowance validation and one ledger-path refresh through the shared allowance boundary in `reference/reconstruction.md` "Spec with ledger" step 4; legacy briefs without tasks omit init, not recovery/migration; render allowance and observed task/ledger state; read `After the loop` and its references; continue from `After the loop` step 1, the gate set per the loop skill's `## Gate set`; let that skill own execution, with no resume-owned gate run; retain whole-diff code review, happy path when triggered, fresh home conformance review and finishing; never start implement or synthesize Gn completion |
| verify without `Ledger:` | verification-before-completion | full conformance gate; nothing carried over |

## Red flags — STOP

- Any `phase_tracker` or `plan_tracker` mutation before the route's entry checks pass and
  every human question is answered.
- `start <phase>` for anything other than brainstorm as the first arming call.
- `complete` on a prior phase during restore (priors are `skip`ped with a `resume:` reason).
- Running `git worktree add` directly, or `cd`-ing to "fix" a cwd mismatch.
- Accepting a free-form prompt as a brief.

## Project overrides
If a gauntlet overrides file exists - checked in order:
`.pi/gauntlet-overrides.md`, `<repo root>/gauntlet-overrides.md`,
`<repo root>/doc/gauntlet-overrides.md`; first found wins - read it once per session - a skill that already has the file's content in context from an earlier skill's read skips the read; a restored session has nothing in context and reads it. Read
and apply `## conventions` whenever present, without a relevance
judgment.
Give this skill's named section precedence over conflicting
`## conventions` rules. Use other relevant sections - by name match,
by topic (routing,
verification, worktrees, etc.), or by workflow convention - to override or
extend the instructions above. Project-local `AGENTS.md` is already in
context - check it for project-specific routing tables, service paths, and
verification commands.

The recognized headings, their readers, and the rules an override cannot change are listed in the [configuration front door](../../README.md#project-specific-overrides); an override extends or replaces the step it names and never lifts this skill's HARD CONSTRAINT or MUST text.

# Handoff brief contract (gauntlet-resume + gauntlet-handoff supplementary)

Consumed by `gauntlet-resume/SKILL.md` (consumer) and `gauntlet-handoff/SKILL.md`
(producer). Grammar lives only here; both skills cite this file and inline none of it
(`scripts/ci.mjs` drift lint). Coupled to pi-cohort's `handoff` skill (pi-cohort >= 7.1.0, #18)
for exactly six headings - `# Handoff:`, `## Intent`, `## Repo state`, `## Decisions`,
`## Open questions`, `## Skills loaded` - and the `## Repo state` fields. `## Process
state` grammar and its consumer rules are owned here. Cohort drift is reconciled here
and nowhere else.

## Brief grammar

Headings, fixed order. A consumer keys on headings, never prose.

```markdown
# Handoff: <one line>
## Intent
## Repo state
## Decisions
## Open questions
## Skills loaded
## Process state
```

| Section | Content | Presence |
|---|---|---|
| `## Repo state` | one field per line: `toplevel`, `worktree: yes <path>` or `worktree: no`, `branch` (`detached` when none), `HEAD`, `base` (`unknown` when no remote resolves), `dirty: <porcelain>` or `dirty: clean`, `diff-stat` (`unavailable` when base unknown), `test cmd`; any field `unavailable` when its command failed; heading `## Repo state: not a git repo` outside git | always |
| `## Decisions` | bullets; rejected alternatives marked `rejected:` | always |
| `## Skills loaded` | frontmatter `name`s; `## Skills loaded: none` when none | always |
| `## Process state` | `phase_tracker status` then `plan_tracker status` verbatim; `Active task: <name|none>`; optional one or more consecutive `PR: <owner/repo#N>` / `Pre-rework head: <40-char sha>` pairs, one per record group, home first, in record order, only for a PR subject; optional single `Rework base: <40-char sha>` after all PR pairs; optional coordinated block defined below after that line; the line `Gate history not restored - re-validate before advancing.` | only when a phase is `in_progress` and no hotfix flow is in context |

For a loop ledger (line 1 exactly `# Ledger - loop engine`), replace `Active task` with these two fields, retaining both tracker status outputs and the gate-history line:

```text
Ledger: <path>
Last decision: <line>
```

Use the ledger path relative to the worktree and the last physical decision line, or `none` for an empty Decisions section. Read the ledger on disk; the brief is a pointer, not a second ledger state carrier. Permit task rows beside a ledger: copy `plan_tracker status` verbatim, including the dispatched row's `in_progress` status and any conformance tasks with their observed statuses. Never infer task state from the brief's prose. Reject a block mixing these fields with `Active task` or missing either loop field.

Consumer rules: process state absent -> plain handoff (the consumer starts its
own process from `## Intent`). Give valid ledger fields precedence over `No plan active.` and run ledger admission. Restore phase-only state for `No plan active.` only with no `Ledger` field. Load named skills as the consumer.

A brief is any text whose first line starts `# Handoff:` - a file on disk or pasted
inline. `## Repo state` is matched by prefix: `## Repo state` or
`## Repo state: not a git repo`.

## Producers

`gauntlet-handoff` is the only writer of `## Process state`; it appends to the file
cohort's `handoff` skill wrote, which ends at `## Skills loaded`. Drop exactly the last
line of the `phase_tracker status` output when it starts with `Context: `; copy the
rest verbatim. Layout, byte-exact: one blank line, the heading on its own line, a
blank line, that phase status, a blank line, the `plan_tracker status` output
verbatim, a blank line,
`Active task: <name|none>`, then, only for a PR subject, one or more consecutive
`PR: <owner/repo#N>` / `Pre-rework head: <40-char sha>` pairs, one per record group,
home first, in record order, then optional single `Rework base: <40-char sha>` after all PR pairs, then the optional coordinated block below, then the gate-history line after the last pair, rework-base line, or block -
unfenced, nothing after.
For a task plan, set `Active task` to the first `→` task name, else `none` (also for `No plan active.`). For a line-1 ledger, read its path and last decision and use the loop alternative above, retaining the optional PR pairs and rework base before the gate-history line. Copy the full rework base only from the top-level record when present; never invent a boundary for incomplete sync. Copy only top-level record pairs, without titles; `Threads:` and record `### PR #<N>` subsections are not brief fields. For N=1 emit one pair; without a Rework record use the ordinary layout.

Example appended block (the fence is documentation; the brief carries no fence):

```text

## Process state

Phases:
  ⊘ brainstorm (resume: <spec path>)
  ⊘ plan (resume: pasted brief)
  → implement(W2)
  ○ verify
  ○ ship

Plan: 1/3 done (1 in progress, 1 pending)

  ✓ [0] W1: contract
  → [1] W2: producer
  ○ [2] W2: consumer

Active task: W2: producer
Gate history not restored - re-validate before advancing.
```

## Coordinated brief grammar

For more than one member only, append this block after the optional PR pairs and before the terminal gate-history line. Emit entries in the home spec's `### Leg:` order, home first. Keep the six core headings and `## Repo state` fields unchanged and bound to the run home. Distinguish PR home (the leading PR pair) from run home (the first member); do not infer one from the other.

```text
legs:
  - repo: repo-a
    worktree: <absolute home worktree>
    branch: <shared branch>
    HEAD: <full sha>
    dirty: clean
  - repo: repo-b
    worktree: missing
    branch: <shared branch>
    HEAD: <last recorded full sha or unavailable>
    dirty: unavailable
    receipt: <absolute home-owned receipt path>
Gate history not restored - re-validate before advancing.
```

Keep fields in this order. Use the portable repo identifier from `../../brainstorming/reference/legs.md`. Record the absolute worktree path or the literal `missing` when absent; record live HEAD and porcelain dirt (`clean` when empty), or last recorded HEAD and `unavailable` dirt for a missing tree. Include the optional receipt path only when a delivery receipt exists; transport is not proof. For a live tree without a receipt omit that field. Single-member and legacy briefs carry no coordinated block, leg file, receipt, `--leg` or companion loop.

## Coordinated admission

Run resume entry check 3 against the run home unchanged. Resolve the home spec through Candidates, retaining human approval/confirmation requirements; artifact presence supplies no approval. Before any tracker write, compare ordered brief membership with the home spec's `### Leg:` blocks exactly; name the missing, extra or reordered leg and both lists on mismatch. Use `../../brainstorming/reference/legs.md` for membership, companion-file and scope grammar; keep no duplicate grammar here.

For each companion, parse the home overrides' selected sibling clone URL with shape-ticket's shared parser and use `<home PRIMARY parent>/<NAME>` as its declared primary. Canonicalize that primary's git common directory. For a brief's `worktree: missing`, apply [Locate a leg tree](../../brainstorming/reference/legs.md#locate-a-leg-tree) using the declared primary and recorded branch. Use a found tree as the companion worktree for the remaining admission checks. On lookup failure, report that rule's repo, branch and reason; state that an empty lookup authorizes no recreation, receipt or approval, retaining live receipt admission below for a missing delivered tree. Keep an explicit brief `worktree:` path as recorded and validate it without replacing it from the lookup. Require the companion worktree's canonical git common directory to equal the declared primary's, its live branch to equal the shared branch, and its leg file's full `**Home:**` tuple to equal the run home's repo, shared branch and repo-relative spec path. Stop naming the offending leg and expected/observed path, branch or full tuple. A live tree's branch or tuple mismatch is not informational drift.

Admit a missing companion tree only after live receipt validation under `../../finishing-a-development-branch/reference/legs.md`. A copied receipt alone proves nothing. Announce per-leg HEAD and dirty drift against live trees without stopping; identify each leg. Keep approval, standing-grant validation, arming order and task snapshots unchanged. Dispatch task `Leg:` work in that leg's checkout, not the home by default.

For a ship-stage retry with a correctly stripped plan, require every companion receipt to validate live before admitting the missing plan. Restore through the legal brainstorm start/skip, plan start/skip and implement skip sequence to verify, without inventing a plan_check stamp or conformance evidence. Re-validate unlanded home using recorded contracts and original scoped ACs; for a ledger subject, recover gate pairs from the committed pre-strip ledger per [finish verification-set.md](../../finishing-a-development-branch/reference/verification-set.md#post-strip-recovery), not the spec's full verification contract. Then run fresh home conformance and finish; use the finishing reference's retry route. Preserve receipts on seal or home delivery failure; do not repair or replace a correctly stripped plan. An absent plan without this fully validated ship retry remains a stop.

## Tracker output grammar

Must match `formatStatus` in the phase-tracker and plan-tracker extensions.

```
Phases:
  ✓ brainstorm
  → implement(W2)
  ○ verify (reason)
```

Glyphs `✓` complete, `→` in_progress, `⊘` skipped, `○` pending; `(reason)` suffix when
set; `name(substep)` only on the in-progress phase.

```
Plan: 2/5 done (1 in progress, 2 pending)

  ✓ [0] <name>
  → [1] <name>
```

or `No plan active.`. Task glyphs `✓` complete, `→` in_progress, `✗` failed, `⊘` skipped,
`○` pending, mapping 1:1 onto `plan_tracker init` `{name, status}` statuses.

For ledger task rows, match the suffix pattern `^(row \d+(?: \(\S+\))?) \| .+$` against the text after `[i] ` and restore only capture 1. Treat everything after the first canonical name's ` | ` as display text, including pipes and row-like text; never derive identity from the description. For example, `row 3 | 2/5: Verify loop behavior and recovery` restores `row 3`. Retain legacy plain names and the numeric prefix form: remove the prefix pattern `^\d+/\d+: ` only when the remainder matches the canonical pattern `^row \d+(?: \(\S+\))?$`. Strip recognized labels before verify/ship `plan_tracker init` and snapshot name comparisons. Keep Gn and every other task name byte-identical, including numeric prefixes on non-ledger names. Never restore labels from a brief: the post-restore refresh recomputes descriptions and allowance from the current spec and ledger, so a changed description or denominator is not drift or a second task.

Parse stops (print the offending line, make no tracker call):

- a task line not matching `^\s*[✓→✗⊘○] \[\d+\] .+$` - the "unparsable process-state
  task line" stop;
- a process-state section whose phase block shows all `○` - contradictory (the producer
  emits the section only with an in-progress phase);
- a phase block with more than one `→` line - contradictory (the tracker holds one active
  phase; print both lines).

## Process-state restore

Before any tracker write, read the optional ordered PR pairs. Fetch branch identity
from the first pair only (home) with
`gh pr view <N> --repo <owner/repo> --json headRefName`. Compare `headRefName` with
`git -C <worktree> branch --show-current`. A mismatch stops with
`brief names PR #N on <headRefName>, worktree is on <branch>`, substituting the observed PR number and both actual branch names, never literal placeholders; a failed fetch stops
with its error. Do not fetch later pairs' branches for this identity check.
Read the worktree spec's `## Rework record` and compare its top-level `PR:` identities
(without titles) with the brief identities in order. A mismatch stops with
`brief lists <brief order>, record lists <record order>`, substituting both observed
ordered lists, before any tracker call. Resolve the spec through reconstruction's
candidate rules below before this comparison; artifact presence supplies no approval.
Carry all paired full pre-rework heads downstream in their original order.
Carry the optional full rework base downstream; reconstruction prefers it over the first pair's head as its scan base. Without optional pairs,
retain ordinary restoration.
Preserve the entry checks, standing-grant validation, plan repair, and task snapshot;
PR identity implies no approval or gate evidence.

Facts that fix the order (from the extensions):

- Arming happens only on `start brainstorm`; `reset` disarms; `skip` and `complete`
  preserve it.
- `plan_check` stamps only inside an armed flow; unarmed it returns
  `PASS (no flow to stamp)`.
- `start implement` is rejected without a current `plan_check` stamp.
- `skip` has no state precondition and takes a `reason`; one phase is active at a time.
- `complete verify` is blocked without a fresh `conformance-reviewer` dispatch when
  closure review is enforced.
- `plan_tracker init` on an in-progress implement with every task `complete`/`skipped`
  auto-completes implement.

Per-stage call table, keyed by the brief's active phase (`→`). Use
`R = resume: <brief file or "pasted brief">` for plan/implement/verify skips and
`S = resume: <spec path>` for brainstorm skips. Resolve `<spec path>` as
`reconstruction.md` "Candidates" does, to an absolute path under the worktree: the single
`*.md` spec added after the candidate base under `flowGuards.specDirs`, or a spec tracked from that base when
a plan added after base pairs with it by basename. Zero specs -> stop; more than one ->
human picks. The consumer carries this path to its entry check 6 and its post-restore
announcement without re-resolving it.

Honor SKILL.md entry check 6's deferred stop before any process-state arming call below; carry the resolved spec path without re-discovery. For brainstorm-stage briefs, resolve any existing spec through these candidate rules and run entry check 6's deferred-header admission before `start brainstorm`; with zero specs, restore brainstorm without a spec. Keep grant decoding exempt for this stage. A handoff after row 4's push succeeded but PR creation failed still has brainstorm in_progress; its deferred header stops restoration, not the ordinary gate.

| Active | Calls, in order |
|---|---|
| brainstorm | `start brainstorm`; `substep` if the brief shows one |
| plan | `start brainstorm`; `skip brainstorm S`; `start plan`; `substep` if shown |
| implement with ledger | Read ledger line 1; resolve its path-only `**Spec:**` header; run entry checks 1-6, naming check 6 (Grant field); `start brainstorm`; `skip brainstorm` reason `resume: <spec path>`; `start plan`; `plan_check` on the absolute ledger path; on PASS `skip plan` reason `resume: <spec> (loop engine)` using the resolved absolute spec path as `<spec>`; `start implement`; pending recovery against the unmigrated ledger, clean-tree migration, final allowance validation, then one ledger-path refresh, no `init`; apply the shared allowance boundary in `reconstruction.md` "Spec with ledger" step 4 before continuation; render allowance, rows and decisions; continue at loop step 5. Follow `reconstruction.md` "Spec with ledger" for this self-contained ordered restore. On FAIL stop with findings, never `## Plan repair` or writing-plans. |
| implement with task plan | `start brainstorm`; `skip brainstorm S`; `start plan`; `plan_check({ planPath })`; on FAIL run `## Plan repair`; on PASS `skip plan R`; `start implement`; `substep` if shown; `plan_tracker init` |
| verify | `start brainstorm`; `skip brainstorm S`; `start plan`; `plan_check({ planPath })`; on FAIL run `## Plan repair`; on PASS `skip plan R`, then `skip implement R`; `start verify`; `substep` if shown; `plan_tracker init`. Never call `start implement`. |
| ship | With a correctly stripped coordinated plan, apply "Coordinated admission"'s fully receipt-validated retry route instead of plan repair; otherwise as verify. Restoration stops at verify in_progress: `complete verify` needs a fresh conformance dispatch and `skip verify` would bypass a real gate. Announce that the closure review re-runs before ship |

Apply reconstruction's pending recovery before dispatch or verification on every ledger restore, including verify/ship. Use the home return contract for a home tuple and the companion protocol only for an actual multi-member companion; record a validated interrupted return before continuing.

For a ledger brief, pair by the ledger's path-only `**Spec:**` header, not basename; require the resolved spec under `flowGuards.specDirs` and the ledger under its sibling plans directory. spec was added after base or tracked from base (`reconstruction.md` "Candidates");
resolve the selected plan to an absolute path under the worktree before `plan_check`.
Zero pairs -> stop; more than one -> human picks.

## Plan repair

Entered from the call table's `implement` row and from `reconstruction.md` "Spec with plan" step 2 when `plan_check` returns FAIL. Inputs: the findings, and the task list with statuses (the brief's, or the confirmed reconstruction snapshot) - read it for evidence, never rewrite it.

Before citation-table classification, route `baseline-line` and substantive `open-questions` findings through the continuation below. Keep the brief's or confirmed reconstruction's task snapshot (names, order, statuses) verbatim throughout; never take writing-plans step 7's fresh-plan initialization.

### Baseline continuation

On `baseline-line` or a substantive baseline-form `open-questions` finding, bring a landed fix named by the brief or human into the worktree through `/skill:using-git-worktrees` "the base branch advances" (rebase, or merge for a shared branch). Without a named fix, proceed directly to the rerun. Dispatch `plan-writer` per `/skill:writing-plans` "Author the plan" step 3: `agent: "plan-writer"`, `context: "fresh"`, `async: false`, `cwd: <absolute worktree>`, `phase: "plan-write"`, `acceptance: { level: "none", reason: "the parent plan_check owns acceptance" }`. Fill its fixed task template with the five absolute paths (worktree, spec, plan, writing-plans SKILL.md, its reference/plan-contract.md), then append `Findings: rerun baseline`. Let the writer run Baseline and regenerate its rows; never synthesize evidence or SHAs. On dispatch error, async handle, or missing/empty plan, stop and report without a parent-authored fallback.

Run `plan_check({ planPath })` in the parent after either child reply. Route the result:

| Result / substantive row | Continuation |
|---|---|
| `PLAN WRITTEN` + `PASS`, section absent or exactly `- none` | Return to the originating restore's remaining steps: call table from `skip plan R` through the appropriate implement/verify continuation (ship restores at verify), or reconstruction step 3. Initialize `plan_tracker` only from the saved task snapshot, never the generated fresh-plan list. |
| `- Task N: ... fails on <sha>` | Present the task, command, base SHA and exit code, then writing-plans step 6's three options, one per line: **fix-first** - `/skill:shape-ticket` for the base failure (its gate applies), then pause; **narrow** - human supplies filter or path text, re-dispatch with `Findings: Task N Tests: narrow to <text>`; **amend** - brainstorming's `reference/amendment-surface.md` section 5. Print a `Recommendation:` line and wait for selection. |
| Global or contamination rows (`Baseline: worktree dirty`, `Baseline: in-flight source edits`, `dirtied tracked source`, `moved HEAD`) | Take writing-plans step 6's restore-and-rerun path, not the menu. Name paths and causes; the parent's own in-flight work uses its own commit step (doc-only paths can be listed under `In-flight:`); ask the human to commit, discard, or move other paths and test-produced dirt. Never clean automatically. After restoration re-dispatch with `Findings: rerun baseline`, then parent check. |
| Other substantive `open-questions` rows (contract questions) | Present the rows, wait for answers, re-dispatch per step 3 with answers in `Findings:`, then parent check and this same return route. |
| Other checks | Use the citation table and its three-round rollback below. |

End a turn awaiting selection, restoration, or answers with phase `plan` retained in_progress and no tracker initialization of any kind. Keep the snapshot for the eventual return. Resolved failure rows disappear only through the writer's Baseline rerun; resume writes no Open Questions rows. Plans without `baseline:` bullets intentionally enter this continuation on their `baseline-line` finding.

### Citation repair

Record the plan's state before any write: tracked and clean when `git -C <worktree> ls-files --error-unmatch -- <plan path>` exits 0 and `git -C <worktree> status --porcelain -- <plan path>` prints nothing (index and working copy both match HEAD; a staged edit alone makes it dirty); otherwise copy the file to a temp path outside the repository before citation repair writes anything. Any non-empty porcelain output, including staged-only `M  <plan path>`, takes this copy path even when tracked and the working copy equals HEAD. Never substitute `git checkout` for the dirty or untracked plan's snapshot or saved-copy restore.

Classify every finding against the table by its `check` and `reason`, gathering the row's evidence first. One finding with no row -> stop (below) before any write.

| Finding (`check`, `reason`) | Evidence | Edit |
|---|---|---|
| `anchor-resolution`, range outside section or line shift | the anchor's heading string matches exactly one current spec heading | set the `**Spec:**` `L<n>-L<m>` range to the current span of that section that holds the task body's existing literals |
| `quote-integrity`, task-owned row | the row's anchor already resolves (repair anchors first) | add the missing backtick literal to the owning task's body; never replace or remove task text |
| `quote-integrity`, `Verification`-owned row | as above | add the missing literal to the header `**Verification:**` line |
| `table-closure`, row anchor not in the owner's `**Spec:**` set | the owner cell names an existing task whose body does the row's requirement | move the row's anchor together with that same owner's `**Spec:**` anchor; the owner cell never changes |
| `paths-exist`, `Modify: path "<p>" does not exist` | the owning task is `complete` or `skipped` in the task list, and `git -C <worktree> log --diff-filter=D --format=%h -1 -- <p>` is non-empty | drop that `Modify:` row |
| `paths-exist` or `tests-block`, a `Test:` path that does not exist or a `Tests:` segment not anchored | `git -C <worktree> log --diff-filter=R --format= --name-status -M -1 -- <old> <new>` shows the rename `<old>` -> `<new>` | substitute `<new>` for `<old>` in the `Test:` line and in the `Tests:` command; nothing else in the command changes |

Every other `check` (`input`, `placeholder-scan`, `header-entrypoint`, `header-happy-path`, `waiver-literal`, `wave-file-disjointness`, `internal`) and every reason not listed (a missing `Files:` block, an invalid or empty glob, a missing or ambiguous heading, a `pending`/`in_progress` owner of a dead `Modify:` row, a command broadening) has no row. Task names, count, order, wave membership, `Solo:` lines, the owner column, and task text beyond an added literal or a substituted path never change.

Loop: write every classified edit, re-run `plan_check({ planPath })`, classify any new finding the same way; at most 3 rounds.

PASS with the plan tracked and clean before the loop -> read [commit-message.md](../../finishing-a-development-branch/reference/commit-message.md), take the entire subject verbatim from its Plan citation repair row, and commit the plan alone with that message on stdin:

```bash
git -C <worktree> add -- <plan path> && git -C <worktree> commit -q -F - -- <plan path>
```

A failed commit stops with git's output. PASS with the plan untracked or dirty before the loop -> leave the repair in the working copy; it lands with the next task commit. Then continue the originating route: the call table from `skip plan R`, or reconstruction step 3.

Stop (a finding with no row, or a finding surviving the third round): when a round wrote the plan, restore its pre-loop bytes (`git -C <worktree> checkout -- <plan path>` when tracked and clean, else the saved copy) - a stop before the first write runs no git command; print the findings (a dead `Modify:` row prefixed with its owning task, e.g. `Task 5:`), leave `plan` in_progress with no `init`, and print one line:

- no row: `Repair stopped: <check> - <reason> is outside citation repair; the plan file is unchanged. Edit the plan (task changes allowed), then re-run /skill:gauntlet-resume.`
- third round: `Repair stopped: <check> - <reason> survived 3 rounds. Edit the plan, then re-run /skill:gauntlet-resume.`

Resume never edits the spec or writes an Open Question itself; the dispatched plan-writer owns generated baseline rows.

"Exact" restoration binds: the active phase identity and substep, and the plan task list
(names, order, statuses) verbatim. Prior phases show `⊘ (resume: ...)` regardless of the
brief's glyph - skip-arming is the mechanism and completing priors would fabricate gated
history. For a ledger, restore the saved mixed list only on verify/ship, then refresh its ledger entries from disk; on implement, refresh without `init`. `No plan active.` -> no `init` call; a ledger still refreshes.

Before `init`, validate feasibility against the tracker's own rules:

- pending-suffix order - every `○` task must trail every non-pending task;
- the implement auto-complete edge - an implement brief whose tasks are all
  complete/skipped is infeasible as stated; propose verify as the target and ask.

Every restore ends with:

```
Gate history not restored; re-validating `<task>` before any stage advance
```

For a ledger, use `ledger rows` as `<task>` and render the current rows and last decision from disk.

For a task plan, `<task>` is the brief's `Active task`, else the first in-progress task, else `none`
(whole-deliverable re-validation). Gate history, closure-review evidence, and fix rounds
are never inferred or restored; a ship-stage brief resumes at verify.

A restore that ran `## Plan repair` prints `Repaired plan: <n> findings (<comma-separated check names, deduplicated>)` on its own line directly before the closing line; the `Standing grant` line (SKILL.md "Post-restore continuation") keeps its place after the closing line. A first-check PASS prints no receipt and makes no commit.

# Handoff brief contract (gauntlet-resume + gauntlet-handoff supplementary)

Consumed by `gauntlet-resume/SKILL.md` (consumer) and `gauntlet-handoff/SKILL.md`
(producer). Grammar lives only here; both skills cite this file and inline none of it
(`scripts/ci.mjs` drift lint). Coupled to pi-cohort's `handoff` skill (pi-cohort >= 7.1.0, #18)
for exactly six headings - `# Handoff:`, `## Intent`, `## Repo state`, `## Decisions`,
`## Open questions`, `## Skills loaded` - and the `## Repo state` fields. `## Process
state` grammar and its consumer rules are owned here. Cohort drift is reconciled here
and nowhere else.

## Brief grammar

Headings, fixed order. A consumer keys on headings, never prose.

```markdown
# Handoff: <one line>
## Intent
## Repo state
## Decisions
## Open questions
## Skills loaded
## Process state
```

| Section | Content | Presence |
|---|---|---|
| `## Repo state` | one field per line: `toplevel`, `worktree: yes <path>` or `worktree: no`, `branch` (`detached` when none), `HEAD`, `base` (`unknown` when no remote resolves), `dirty: <porcelain>` or `dirty: clean`, `diff-stat` (`unavailable` when base unknown), `test cmd`; any field `unavailable` when its command failed; heading `## Repo state: not a git repo` outside git | always |
| `## Decisions` | bullets; rejected alternatives marked `rejected:` | always |
| `## Skills loaded` | frontmatter `name`s; `## Skills loaded: none` when none | always |
| `## Process state` | `phase_tracker status` then `plan_tracker status` verbatim; `Active task: <name|none>`; optional one or more consecutive `PR: <owner/repo#N>` / `Pre-rework head: <40-char sha>` pairs, one per record group, home first, in record order, only for a PR subject; optional single `Rework base: <40-char sha>` after all PR pairs; optional coordinated block defined below after that line; the line `Gate history not restored - re-validate before advancing.` | only when a phase is `in_progress` and no hotfix flow is in context |

```text
Ledger: <path>
Last decision: <line>
```

Consumer rules: process state absent -> plain handoff (the consumer starts its
own process from `## Intent`). Give valid ledger fields precedence over `No plan active.` and run ledger admission. Restore phase-only state for `No plan active.` only with no `Ledger` field. Load named skills as the consumer.

A brief is any text whose first line starts `# Handoff:` - a file on disk or pasted
inline. `## Repo state` is matched by prefix: `## Repo state` or
`## Repo state: not a git repo`.

## Producers

line of the `phase_tracker status` output when it starts with `Context: `; copy the
rest verbatim. Layout, byte-exact: one blank line, the heading on its own line, a
blank line, that phase status, a blank line, the `plan_tracker status` output
verbatim, a blank line,
`Active task: <name|none>`, then, only for a PR subject, one or more consecutive
`PR: <owner/repo#N>` / `Pre-rework head: <40-char sha>` pairs, one per record group,
home first, in record order, then optional single `Rework base: <40-char sha>` after all PR pairs, then the optional coordinated block below, then the gate-history line after the last pair, rework-base line, or block -
unfenced, nothing after.

Example appended block (the fence is documentation; the brief carries no fence):

```text

Phases:

  → implement(W2)
  ○ verify
  ○ ship

Gate history not restored - re-validate before advancing.

## Tracker output grammar

Must match `formatStatus` in the phase-tracker and plan-tracker extensions.

```

  ✓ brainstorm
  → implement(W2)
  ○ verify (reason)
```

Glyphs `✓` complete, `→` in_progress, `⊘` skipped, `○` pending; `(reason)` suffix when
set; `name(substep)` only on the in-progress phase.

```
Plan: 2/5 done (1 in progress, 2 pending)

  ✓ [0] <name>
  → [1] <name>
```

or `No plan active.`. Task glyphs `✓` complete, `→` in_progress, `✗` failed, `⊘` skipped,

- a process-state section whose phase block shows all `○` - contradictory (the producer

| Result / substantive row | Continuation |
|---|---|
| `PLAN WRITTEN` + `PASS`, section absent or exactly `- none` | Return to the originating restore's remaining steps: call table from `skip plan R` through the appropriate implement/verify continuation (ship restores at verify), or reconstruction step 3. Initialize `plan_tracker` only from the saved task snapshot, never the generated fresh-plan list. |
| `- Task N: ... fails on <sha>` | Present the task, command, base SHA and exit code, then writing-plans step 6's three options, one per line: **fix-first** - `/skill:shape-ticket` for the base failure (its gate applies), then pause; **narrow** - human supplies filter or path text, re-dispatch with `Findings: Task N Tests: narrow to <text>`; **amend** - brainstorming's `reference/amendment-surface.md` section 5. Print a `Recommendation:` line and wait for selection. |
| Global or contamination rows (`Baseline: worktree dirty`, `Baseline: in-flight source edits`, `dirtied tracked source`, `moved HEAD`) | Take writing-plans step 6's restore-and-rerun path, not the menu. Name paths and causes; the parent's own in-flight work uses its own commit step (doc-only paths can be listed under `In-flight:`); ask the human to commit, discard, or move other paths and test-produced dirt. Never clean automatically. After restoration re-dispatch with `Findings: rerun baseline`, then parent check. |
| Other substantive `open-questions` rows (contract questions) | Present the rows, wait for answers, re-dispatch per step 3 with answers in `Findings:`, then parent check and this same return route. |
| Other checks | Use the citation table and its three-round rollback below. |

End a turn awaiting selection, restoration, or answers with phase `plan` retained in_progress and no tracker initialization of any kind. Keep the snapshot for the eventual return. Resolved failure rows disappear only through the writer's Baseline rerun; resume writes no Open Questions rows. Plans without `baseline:` bullets intentionally enter this continuation on their `baseline-line` finding.

### Citation repair

Record the plan's state before any write: tracked and clean when `git -C <worktree> ls-files --error-unmatch -- <plan path>` exits 0 and `git -C <worktree> status --porcelain -- <plan path>` prints nothing (index and working copy both match HEAD; a staged edit alone makes it dirty); otherwise copy the file to a temp path outside the repository before citation repair writes anything. Any non-empty porcelain output, including staged-only `M  <plan path>`, takes this copy path even when tracked and the working copy equals HEAD. Never substitute `git checkout` for the dirty or untracked plan's snapshot or saved-copy restore.

Classify every finding against the table by its `check` and `reason`, gathering the row's evidence first. One finding with no row -> stop (below) before any write.

| Finding (`check`, `reason`) | Evidence | Edit |
|---|---|---|
| `anchor-resolution`, range outside section or line shift | the anchor's heading string matches exactly one current spec heading | set the `**Spec:**` `L<n>-L<m>` range to the current span of that section that holds the task body's existing literals |
| `quote-integrity`, task-owned row | the row's anchor already resolves (repair anchors first) | add the missing backtick literal to the owning task's body; never replace or remove task text |
| `quote-integrity`, `Verification`-owned row | as above | add the missing literal to the header `**Verification:**` line |
| `table-closure`, row anchor not in the owner's `**Spec:**` set | the owner cell names an existing task whose body does the row's requirement | move the row's anchor together with that same owner's `**Spec:**` anchor; the owner cell never changes |
| `paths-exist`, `Modify: path "<p>" does not exist` | the owning task is `complete` or `skipped` in the task list, and `git -C <worktree> log --diff-filter=D --format=%h -1 -- <p>` is non-empty | drop that `Modify:` row |
| `paths-exist` or `tests-block`, a `Test:` path that does not exist or a `Tests:` segment not anchored | `git -C <worktree> log --diff-filter=R --format= --name-status -M -1 -- <old> <new>` shows the rename `<old>` -> `<new>` | substitute `<new>` for `<old>` in the `Test:` line and in the `Tests:` command; nothing else in the command changes |

Every other `check` (`input`, `placeholder-scan`, `header-entrypoint`, `header-happy-path`, `waiver-literal`, `wave-file-disjointness`, `internal`) and every reason not listed (a missing `Files:` block, an invalid or empty glob, a missing or ambiguous heading, a `pending`/`in_progress` owner of a dead `Modify:` row, a command broadening) has no row. Task names, count, order, wave membership, `Solo:` lines, the owner column, and task text beyond an added literal or a substituted path never change.

Loop: write every classified edit, re-run `plan_check({ planPath })`, classify any new finding the same way; at most 3 rounds.

PASS with the plan tracked and clean before the loop -> read [commit-message.md](../../finishing-a-development-branch/reference/commit-message.md), take the entire subject verbatim from its Plan citation repair row, and commit the plan alone with that message on stdin:

```bash
git -C <worktree> add -- <plan path> && git -C <worktree> commit -q -F - -- <plan path>
```

A failed commit stops with git's output. PASS with the plan untracked or dirty before the loop -> leave the repair in the working copy; it lands with the next task commit. Then continue the originating route: the call table from `skip plan R`, or reconstruction step 3.

Stop (a finding with no row, or a finding surviving the third round): when a round wrote the plan, restore its pre-loop bytes (`git -C <worktree> checkout -- <plan path>` when tracked and clean, else the saved copy) - a stop before the first write runs no git command; print the findings (a dead `Modify:` row prefixed with its owning task, e.g. `Task 5:`), leave `plan` in_progress with no `init`, and print one line:

- no row: `Repair stopped: <check> - <reason> is outside citation repair; the plan file is unchanged. Edit the plan (task changes allowed), then re-run /skill:gauntlet-resume.`
- third round: `Repair stopped: <check> - <reason> survived 3 rounds. Edit the plan, then re-run /skill:gauntlet-resume.`

Resume never edits the spec or writes an Open Question itself; the dispatched plan-writer owns generated baseline rows.

"Exact" restoration binds: the active phase identity and substep, and the plan task list
(names, order, statuses) verbatim. Prior phases show `⊘ (resume: ...)` regardless of the
brief's glyph - skip-arming is the mechanism and completing priors would fabricate gated
history. For a ledger, restore the saved mixed list only on verify/ship, then refresh its ledger entries from disk; on implement, refresh without `init`. `No plan active.` -> no `init` call; a ledger still refreshes.

Before `init`, validate feasibility against the tracker's own rules:

- pending-suffix order - every `○` task must trail every non-pending task;
- the implement auto-complete edge - an implement brief whose tasks are all
  complete/skipped is infeasible as stated; propose verify as the target and ask.

Every restore ends with:

```
Gate history not restored; re-validating `<task>` before any stage advance
```

For a ledger, use `ledger rows` as `<task>` and render the current rows and last decision from disk.

For a task plan, `<task>` is the brief's `Active task`, else the first in-progress task, else `none`
(whole-deliverable re-validation). Gate history, closure-review evidence, and fix rounds
are never inferred or restored; a ship-stage brief resumes at verify.

A restore that ran `## Plan repair` prints `Repaired plan: <n> findings (<comma-separated check names, deduplicated>)` on its own line directly before the closing line; the `Standing grant` line (SKILL.md "Post-restore continuation") keeps its place after the closing line. A first-check PASS prints no receipt and makes no commit.

# Handoff brief contract (gauntlet-resume + gauntlet-handoff supplementary)

Consumed by `gauntlet-resume/SKILL.md` (consumer) and `gauntlet-handoff/SKILL.md`
(producer). Grammar lives only here; both skills cite this file and inline none of it
(`scripts/ci.mjs` drift lint). Coupled to pi-cohort's `handoff` skill (pi-cohort >= 7.1.0, #18)
for exactly six headings - `# Handoff:`, `## Intent`, `## Repo state`, `## Decisions`,
`## Open questions`, `## Skills loaded` - and the `## Repo state` fields. `## Process
state` grammar and its consumer rules are owned here. Cohort drift is reconciled here
and nowhere else.

## Brief grammar

Headings, fixed order. A consumer keys on headings, never prose.

```markdown
# Handoff: <one line>
## Intent
## Repo state
## Decisions
## Open questions
## Skills loaded
## Process state
```

| Section | Content | Presence |
|---|---|---|
| `## Repo state` | one field per line: `toplevel`, `worktree: yes <path>` or `worktree: no`, `branch` (`detached` when none), `HEAD`, `base` (`unknown` when no remote resolves), `dirty: <porcelain>` or `dirty: clean`, `diff-stat` (`unavailable` when base unknown), `test cmd`; any field `unavailable` when its command failed; heading `## Repo state: not a git repo` outside git | always |
| `## Decisions` | bullets; rejected alternatives marked `rejected:` | always |
| `## Skills loaded` | frontmatter `name`s; `## Skills loaded: none` when none | always |
| `## Process state` | `phase_tracker status` then `plan_tracker status` verbatim; `Active task: <name|none>`; optional one or more consecutive `PR: <owner/repo#N>` / `Pre-rework head: <40-char sha>` pairs, one per record group, home first, in record order, only for a PR subject; optional single `Rework base: <40-char sha>` after all PR pairs; optional coordinated block defined below after that line; the line `Gate history not restored - re-validate before advancing.` | only when a phase is `in_progress` and no hotfix flow is in context |

For a loop ledger (line 1 exactly `# Ledger - loop engine`), replace `Active task` with these two fields, retaining both tracker status outputs and the gate-history line:

```text
Ledger: <path>
Last decision: <line>
```

Use the ledger path relative to the worktree and the last physical decision line, or `none` for an empty Decisions section. Read the ledger on disk; the brief is a pointer, not a second ledger state carrier. Permit task rows beside a ledger: copy `plan_tracker status` verbatim, including the dispatched row's `in_progress` status and any conformance tasks with their observed statuses. Never infer task state from the brief's prose. Reject a block mixing these fields with `Active task` or missing either loop field.

Consumer rules: process state absent -> plain handoff (the consumer starts its
own process from `## Intent`). Give valid ledger fields precedence over `No plan active.` and run ledger admission. Restore phase-only state for `No plan active.` only with no `Ledger` field. Load named skills as the consumer.

A brief is any text whose first line starts `# Handoff:` - a file on disk or pasted
inline. `## Repo state` is matched by prefix: `## Repo state` or
`## Repo state: not a git repo`.

## Producers

`gauntlet-handoff` is the only writer of `## Process state`; it appends to the file
cohort's `handoff` skill wrote, which ends at `## Skills loaded`. Drop exactly the last
line of the `phase_tracker status` output when it starts with `Context: `; copy the
rest verbatim. Layout, byte-exact: one blank line, the heading on its own line, a
blank line, that phase status, a blank line, the `plan_tracker status` output
verbatim, a blank line,
`Active task: <name|none>`, then, only for a PR subject, one or more consecutive
`PR: <owner/repo#N>` / `Pre-rework head: <40-char sha>` pairs, one per record group,
home first, in record order, then optional single `Rework base: <40-char sha>` after all PR pairs, then the optional coordinated block below, then the gate-history line after the last pair, rework-base line, or block -
unfenced, nothing after.
For a task plan, set `Active task` to the first `→` task name, else `none` (also for `No plan active.`). For a line-1 ledger, read its path and last decision and use the loop alternative above, retaining the optional PR pairs and rework base before the gate-history line. Copy the full rework base only from the top-level record when present; never invent a boundary for incomplete sync. Copy only top-level record pairs, without titles; `Threads:` and record `### PR #<N>` subsections are not brief fields. For N=1 emit one pair; without a Rework record use the ordinary layout.

Example appended block (the fence is documentation; the brief carries no fence):

```text

## Process state

Phases:

  ⊘ plan (resume: pasted brief)
  → implement(W2)
  ○ verify

Active task: W2: producer

For more than one member only, append this block after the optional PR pairs and before the terminal gate-history line. Emit entries in the home spec's `### Leg:` order, home first. Keep the six core headings and `## Repo state` fields unchanged and bound to the run home. Distinguish PR home (the leading PR pair) from run home (the first member); do not infer one from the other.

```text
legs:

```

## Coordinated admission

Before any tracker write, compare ordered brief membership with the home spec's `### Leg:` blocks exactly; name the missing, extra or reordered leg and both lists on mismatch. Use `../../brainstorming/reference/legs.md` for membership, companion-file and scope grammar; keep no duplicate grammar here.

Announce per-leg HEAD and dirty drift against live trees without stopping; identify each leg. Keep approval, standing-grant validation, arming order and task snapshots unchanged. For a ship-stage retry with a correctly stripped plan, require every companion receipt to validate live before admitting the missing plan. Then run fresh home conformance and finish; use the finishing reference's retry route. Preserve receipts on seal or home delivery failure; do not repair or replace a correctly stripped plan. ## Tracker output grammar

Must match `formatStatus` in the phase-tracker and plan-tracker extensions.

```
Phases:
  ✓ brainstorm
  → implement(W2)
  ○ verify (reason)
```

Glyphs `✓` complete, `→` in_progress, `⊘` skipped, `○` pending; `(reason)` suffix when
set; `name(substep)` only on the in-progress phase.

```
Plan: 2/5 done (1 in progress, 2 pending)

  ✓ [0] <name>
  → [1] <name>
```

or `No plan active.`. Task glyphs `✓` complete, `→` in_progress, `✗` failed, `⊘` skipped,
`○` pending, mapping 1:1 onto `plan_tracker init` `{name, status}` statuses.

For ledger task rows, match the suffix pattern `^(row \d+(?: \(\S+\))?) \| .+$` against the text after `[i] ` and restore only capture 1. Treat everything after the first canonical name's ` | ` as display text, including pipes and row-like text; never derive identity from the description. For example, `row 3 | 2/5: Verify loop behavior and recovery` restores `row 3`. Retain legacy plain names and the numeric prefix form: remove the prefix pattern `^\d+/\d+: ` only when the remainder matches the canonical pattern `^row \d+(?: \(\S+\))?$`. Strip recognized labels before verify/ship `plan_tracker init` and snapshot name comparisons. Keep Gn and every other task name byte-identical, including numeric prefixes on non-ledger names. Never restore labels from a brief: the post-restore refresh recomputes descriptions and allowance from the current spec and ledger, so a changed description or denominator is not drift or a second task.

Parse stops (print the offending line, make no tracker call):

- a task line not matching `^\s*[✓→✗⊘○] \[\d+\] .+$` - the "unparsable process-state
  task line" stop;
- a process-state section whose phase block shows all `○` - contradictory (the producer
  emits the section only with an in-progress phase);
- a phase block with more than one `→` line - contradictory (the tracker holds one active
  phase; print both lines).

## Process-state restore

Before any tracker write, read the optional ordered PR pairs. Fetch branch identity
from the first pair only (home) with
`gh pr view <N> --repo <owner/repo> --json headRefName`. Compare `headRefName` with
`git -C <worktree> branch --show-current`. A mismatch stops with
`brief names PR #N on <headRefName>, worktree is on <branch>`, substituting the observed PR number and both actual branch names, never literal placeholders; a failed fetch stops
with its error. Do not fetch later pairs' branches for this identity check.
Read the worktree spec's `## Rework record` and compare its top-level `PR:` identities
(without titles) with the brief identities in order. A mismatch stops with
`brief lists <brief order>, record lists <record order>`, substituting both observed
ordered lists, before any tracker call. Resolve the spec through reconstruction's
candidate rules below before this comparison; artifact presence supplies no approval.
Carry all paired full pre-rework heads downstream in their original order.
Carry the optional full rework base downstream; reconstruction prefers it over the first pair's head as its scan base. Without optional pairs,
retain ordinary restoration.
Preserve the entry checks, standing-grant validation, plan repair, and task snapshot;
PR identity implies no approval or gate evidence.

Facts that fix the order (from the extensions):

- Arming happens only on `start brainstorm`; `reset` disarms; `skip` and `complete`
  preserve it.
- `plan_check` stamps only inside an armed flow; unarmed it returns
  `PASS (no flow to stamp)`.
- `start implement` is rejected without a current `plan_check` stamp.
- `skip` has no state precondition and takes a `reason`; one phase is active at a time.
- `complete verify` is blocked without a fresh `conformance-reviewer` dispatch when
  closure review is enforced.
- `plan_tracker init` on an in-progress implement with every task `complete`/`skipped`
  auto-completes implement.

For brainstorm-stage briefs, resolve any existing spec through these candidate rules and run entry check 6's deferred-header admission before `start brainstorm`; with zero specs, restore brainstorm without a spec.
